original_question: If X is a Banach space whose bidual X** is Plichko, must X itself be Plichko?
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 6.8 ([59, Question 6.14]): "Let X be a Banach space such that X** is Plichko. Must X be Plichko?" ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact ambient object (a Banach space X), the exact hypothesis (X** is Plichko), and the exact conclusion being asked (whether X must be Plichko). It is essentially the paper's Problem 6.8 verbatim. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
missing_details: To make the question fully stand-alone, unpack "Plichko" in the paper's operative language: Section 3 introduces λ-Plichko spaces via countably λ-norming Markushevich bases, and Section 6 treats the heredity problem for Plichko spaces as the countably norming analogue of the norming-M-basis heredity problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
State explicitly that X** is the Banach bidual of X with its usual bidual norm; the paper leaves this as standard background. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))

Make explicit that no extra hypotheses are assumed: Problem 6.8 does not add separability, Asplundness, WCG, reflexivity, complementedness, or subspace assumptions. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))

If desired, note the paper's scope/context: this is presented as an open particular case of the general heredity problem for Plichko spaces, and specifically as the analogue of the classical question whether WCG is inherited from the bidual. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
refined_question: Let X be a Banach space. If its bidual X** is Plichko, i.e. if X** admits a countably norming Markushevich basis, must X itself be Plichko?
justification: Section 6 first recalls the general heredity problem for Plichko spaces in Problem 6.6, then says that some particular cases remain open, and singles out exactly the bidual case as Problem 6.8. Section 3 supplies the needed paper-faithful meaning of the term "Plichko." So the sharp refinement is simply Problem 6.8 with that term unpacked; it should not be broadened to the general subspace problem or the complemented-subspace problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
